title: How to Get Birds Out of a Dryer Vent
h1: How Do You Get Birds Out of a Dryer Vent Without Hurting Them?
description: Hearing chirping or scratching in your dryer vent? Learn how to get birds out safely, clean out the nest, and keep them from moving back in next spring.
quick_answer: Stop using the dryer, check whether there are eggs or chicks, and give adult birds a chance to leave on their own. Once the vent is empty, pull out the nest, clean the full duct run, and cover the outside opening with a bird-proof vent cap so they can't get back in.
body:
Birds love dryer vents. The opening is sheltered, the duct is warm, and lint makes ready-made nesting material. Getting them out is usually simple, but doing it the wrong way can hurt the birds, leave a fire hazard behind, or just invite them right back.

How do you know a bird is in your dryer vent?

Most people notice the sound first. Chirping, fluttering or scratching near the laundry room wall is a strong clue, especially in spring. Other signs to watch for:

  • Twigs, grass or feathers sticking out of the exterior vent hood
  • Birds flying in and out of the vent on the side of the house or on the roof
  • Clothes taking two or three cycles to dry
  • The dryer or laundry room feeling hotter than usual
  • A musty or burning smell when the dryer runs

Those last three mean airflow is blocked. A nest packed with lint is a real fire risk, so stop using the dryer until the vent is cleared.

What's the safest way to get the birds out?

Start by figuring out what you're dealing with. Look into the vent hood with a flashlight from outside. If you see an adult bird coming and going but no babies, you can usually encourage it to leave:

  1. Turn the dryer off and leave it off. Never run hot air on a nest to flush birds out.
  2. Wait until the adult leaves to feed, which happens many times a day.
  3. Gently remove loose nesting material you can reach from outside, wearing gloves.
  4. Tape a piece of cardboard loosely over the opening for a few hours to see if anything is still inside. If you hear movement, remove it and let the bird out.

If there are eggs or chicks, it's a different situation. Many wild birds are protected by federal law, and moving an active nest can be illegal. The most common approach is to wait a few weeks until the young birds fledge, then clean out the vent. If waiting isn't an option, contact a local wildlife rescue for advice before you touch anything.

How do you clean out the nest once the birds are gone?

Birds don't just build at the opening. They often stuff material several feet back into the duct, and lint collects behind it. Pulling out what you can see at the hood is rarely enough.

A proper cleanout means disconnecting the dryer, running a brush or rotary cleaning tool through the entire duct from the dryer side to the exterior, and vacuuming out the debris. Nests also carry mites and droppings, so wear gloves and a mask and wash up afterward. If the duct is flexible foil and got crushed or torn during the process, replace it with rigid or semi-rigid metal duct.

In a lot of San Diego and Orange County homes the dryer vents out through the roof or a long run through the attic, which makes a full cleanout harder to do yourself. That's where our dryer vent cleaning service comes in. We clear the whole line and check the airflow at the hood when we're done.

How do you keep birds out of the dryer vent for good?

The fix is a better exterior cover. Many homes still have a basic louvered hood with flaps that stick open once they get coated in lint, which gives birds an easy way in. Good options include:

  • A bird-proof vent cap with a spring-loaded or gravity damper that closes tight when the dryer is off
  • A guard designed for dryer vents, with openings large enough that lint can pass through
  • Regular cleaning so the damper keeps closing properly

Avoid putting fine window screen or hardware cloth over a dryer vent. Lint builds up on it fast and blocks the exhaust, which is the same fire risk you were trying to solve. Any guard you add needs to be checked and cleared every few months.

When should you call a professional?

Call for help if the nest is deep in the duct, the vent exits on a second story or roof, the duct is damaged, or the dryer keeps running hot after you've cleared what you can see. A technician can remove the debris from the full length of the vent, repair or replace crushed sections, and install a proper cap so you're not dealing with the same problem next spring.
faqs: Is it dangerous to run the dryer with a bird nest in the vent?

Yes. A nest blocks airflow, which makes the dryer overheat and lets lint pile up near hot surfaces. That's a fire risk, and it can also push moist, hot air back into the laundry room. Stop using the dryer until the vent is clear.
Can I remove a bird nest with eggs in my dryer vent?

Be careful. Many wild bird species are protected, and disturbing an active nest with eggs or chicks can break federal law. The usual answer is to wait until the young leave, which typically takes a few weeks, then clean the vent and add a cover. A local wildlife rescue can advise you if you can't wait.
What time of year do birds nest in dryer vents?
Spring is the busiest season, roughly March through early summer, but in Southern California's mild climate some birds nest earlier or later. Checking your vent cover in late winter is a good habit.
Will a vent cover cause lint to clog?
A fine mesh screen will. Choose a cover made for dryer exhaust, such as a damper-style cap, and check it a few times a year so lint doesn't build up and restrict airflow.
